solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clothing in school leading to grumble

parts.note: SCH is the standard abbreviation for school
to mutter is to grumble under one's breath

explanation.surface: A school uniform that pupils love to complain about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading to' just places the school abbreviation in front of the grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmutter is Yiddish-derived slang, used in the British rag trade, for clothes or cloth.

clue.text: Robbery with violence: do this to find a brigand? Not I

parts.note: 'this' stands for the first word of the answer itself, which also serves as the mixing instruction

indicators.note: 'this' points back at the answer's own first word, a verb meaning to break into pieces, which is what is done to the phrase
'Not I' tells the solver to drop that single letter from the phrase before it

parts.note: taken as written, before the I is dropped

explanation.surface: A violent robbery in which a bandit is caught, with a denial of involvement.
explanation.walkthrough: Smash 'a brigand' without its I and the letters give AND GRAB; put the smashing word in front and the clue describes its own answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-and-grab is a theft in which a shop window is broken and goods snatched, a raid involving force.

clue.text: Robot dog I avoided by rearing inside

indicators.note: inside says the reversed word sits within the shortened dog
a letter that is avoided is left out of the word it belongs to

parts.note: a corgi is a breed of dog; with I taken out it leaves CORG

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing means standing up, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned upwards

explanation.surface: A robot dog stands up on its hind legs without its owner nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I avoided' removes the I from the dog breed, leaving CORG to hold the upturned BY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyborg is a part-human, part-machine being, close kin to a robot in science fiction.

clue.text: H-hooter making one laugh

parts.note: taken as written: the stammered first letter
an owl is a hooter, the bird that hoots

explanation.surface: A stammered 'h-hooter' is so silly it makes someone laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter is not decoration: the H before the hyphen is the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A howl is a loud burst of laughter, so one howl is one laugh.

clue.text: Month in Siam wandering round for flowering plant

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go about the month abbreviation
something wandering does not keep a fixed path, so the country's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the old name of Thailand
MO is short for month

explanation.surface: Spending a month travelling around Thailand in search of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a plant of the pea family with fluffy yellow flowers and touch-sensitive leaves.

clue.text: Chirp

parts.note: the bare definition of the competition word
in a plain competition puzzle solvers write this clue themselves, so only a definition is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was the competition word: Azed gives only a definition, and entrants submit their own cryptic clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is the short high call of a small bird, the same sound as a chirp.

clue.text: It's associated with trash being flogged, blowzy

indicators.note: something flogged is beaten about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the 's that follows is the verb is, part of the joining phrase
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slovenly look goes with cheap rubbish being sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' reads as selling, but it is the beating that mixes the letters. Chambers gives only 'sharp-tasting' for this word; the OED supports 'tarty', the sense needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowzy means coarse and slatternly in looks, and tartish means somewhat tarty, cheap and showy.

clue.text: Understanding what gets pair of nets entangled with barge's stern

indicators.note: things entangled are twisted together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: two copies of the word nets' singular, side by side
the stern of barge is its final letter

explanation.surface: Fishermen's nets get tangled round the back of a barge.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Weed in the Munros maybe, conked out

indicators.note: out suggests something knocked flat or broken, so the word's letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber passes out among weeds on a Scottish mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Munros are Scotland's mountains over 3,000 feet, standing for Scotland, where this word is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Docken is the Scots name for the dock, a broad-leaved weed.

clue.text: Clock in square went round

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for square
'went' is a euphemism for urinated
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone clocking in at a town square and walking around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock in' looks like the start of a shift; the definition is the first word alone. 'went' is used in the toilet sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedo is short for speedometer, the dial a driver informally calls the clock.

clue.text: What's sent Ted crazy with love, captivated by Liz?

definitions.text: What's sent Ted crazy with love, captivated by Liz?

indicators.note: captivated by says the mixture is held prisoner inside the name

parts.note: Bess and Liz are both pet forms of Elizabeth

indicators.note: crazy means disordered, so the letters before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis, so the round letter

explanation.surface: Ted has been driven mad by love for a woman called Liz.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Ted's infatuation with Liz is exactly the state of being besotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Besottedness is the state of being infatuated, the madness of love that has gripped Ted.

clue.text: A trim body, rippling? Could be brat, so muscly

indicators.note: rippling describes moving waves, so the phrase's letters shift into a new order
the rippled phrase could be the brat plus the answer, so the brat must be taken away to leave it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A lean body with rippling muscles, perhaps belonging to a cocky youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: A TRIM BODY rearranged equals BRAT plus the answer, so remove BRAT's letters and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Myoid is a technical adjective for resembling or relating to muscle.

clue.text: The old despair with a phone that's out of order

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: a device out of order is not working properly, so its letters are put in a different sequence

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Despair at having a telephone that is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks the definition as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanhope is an obsolete word for hopelessness, built from wan- meaning lacking and hope.

clue.text: Green tops? The tops indeed

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
to top and to ice are both slang for to kill

explanation.surface: A question about green tops answered that they are the very best.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'tops' is a verb meaning kills; the second is a noun meaning peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertices are the highest points or apexes of figures, so they are the tops.

clue.text: Sage unaccompanied by that last bit of onion

parts.note: solo means performing alone, unaccompanied

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its closing letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of onion

explanation.surface: A herb, sage, served without the onion that usually goes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage and onion is a classic stuffing, which makes 'Sage' read as the herb; it is the wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon was an Athenian lawgiver whose name is used for any wise statesman, a sage.

clue.text: A tin shed like this? Ikea's not involved

indicators.note: involved means twisted or tangled, so the letters are rearranged
the fodder must not include the letters named at the start of the clue, so they are taken out

parts.note: taken as written: the whole phrase is the fodder
taken as written: these letters are cast off

explanation.surface: A flat-pack tin shed, which the furniture store had nothing to do with.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus A TIN rearranges to IKEA'S NOT. Ikea is the Swedish flat-pack furniture chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeo is an Orkney and Shetland hut for drying fish, a shed of stone rather than metal.

clue.text: With resin applied and money invested, offering over-optimistic prospects

indicators.note: money invested is put into something, so it goes inside the other piece

parts.note: roset is a Scots word for resin, used as a verb meaning to rub with resin
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A violinist's bow is rosined and money invested in a hopeful venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose-tinted describes a view that sees things as better than they are, as through rosy spectacles.

clue.text: Horror-struck commanders facing end of engagement

parts.note: an agha is an Ottoman military commander

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the closing letter of engagement

explanation.surface: Military commanders appalled as a battle reaches its close.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock, horror-struck.

clue.text: Punch causing blood to spread from below

parts.note: sang is an old word for blood, as in sang-froid

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from below means reading the word upwards

parts.note: to air is to spread news abroad

explanation.surface: A punch makes blood spread up from beneath a bruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a blow; it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and soda.

clue.text: Sign which restricts self-confidence (7, two words)

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns
ego is one's sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: A signal that keeps a person's self-assurance in check.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goat is Capricorn, a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: One commands no respect, plenty being withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tons is informal for plenty

explanation.surface: A leader commands little respect once a large amount is pulled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One commands' reads like a leader; the definition is a person who commands, that is earns, no respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A snot is slang for a contemptible, snooty person nobody respects.

clue.text: Section in buff uniform wheeling satisfyingly

indicators.note: wheeling means turning about, so the run is read backwards
a section in a phrase is a run of its letters taken from inside it

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words, from the end of the first into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A squad in khaki uniform wheels round on parade to everyone's satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuff is a slangy form of enough, as in 'nuff said', meaning to a satisfying degree.

clue.text: Pair wanting company going round in what commuters take?

indicators.note: going round says the shortened word wraps about the following word
wanting means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a couple is a pair
CO is the abbreviation for company, the part removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple without companions travelling about in the rush-hour crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The up line is the railway track running towards the main city terminus, used by commuters going to work.

clue.text: Drudgery alternating with former rail company, widen out

indicators.note: alternating means taking turns, so letters of the two words are placed one after another in turn

parts.note: first letter of fag, British slang for wearisome toil
first letter of LNE, the London and North Eastern Railway, merged away in 1948
second letter of fag
second letter of LNE
third letter of fag
third letter of LNE

explanation.surface: Tedious work on an old railway line, broadening the track.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG (drudgery) and LNE (the old rail company) take turns letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To flange is to spread out into a projecting rim, so to widen out.

clue.text: Mysterious goddess, endlessly angry but cold inside

indicators.note: inside says the temperature letter goes within the shortened word
endlessly means the word's last letter is cut off

parts.note: heated means angry; without its last letter it leaves HEATE
C stands for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An enigmatic goddess, furious on the outside but cold within.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, night and the underworld, a figure of mystery.

clue.text: Constant upward drift? It was especially noticeable in shires

definitions.text: It was especially noticeable in shires

parts.note: C is the usual symbol for a constant

indicators.note: in a down clue, upward means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: tenor means general drift or meaning

explanation.surface: A steady movement of people towards the rural counties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shires' looks like English counties, but it means Shire horses, the big draught horses whose hoof hair is so obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Cronet is an old word for the coronet, the hair at the top of a horse's hoof, very prominent on Shires.

clue.text: Tag, last to take the lead in Highland trudge

indicators.note: the final letter moves up to become the first, rotating the word

parts.note: an aiglet is the tag on the end of a lace

explanation.surface: A game of tag, with the straggler taking the lead on a Highland trek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tag' reads like the playground game, but it is the tag of a shoelace.
explanation.definitionFit: Taigle is a Scots verb meaning to trudge or to dawdle, hence Highland.

clue.text: Design song about extraterrestrial orreries?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two words go round the alien

parts.note: a plan is a design
ET is the film's extraterrestrial
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Writing a tune about aliens for a display of model planets.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system; planetaria is a plural for such models.

clue.text: King's companion in Elizabethan England

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A royal companion at court in the age of Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was an Anglo-Saxon or Scottish noble holding land from the king, his follower.

clue.text: What's youngster after end of fagging?

definitions.text: What's youngster after end of fagging?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of fagging
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: How a junior pupil feels once fagging is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: fagging was the public-school system of juniors serving seniors, and a boy freed from it is glad.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad means pleased, how a boy feels when his menial duties are finished.

clue.text: Showy bird making an impact after entering

parts.note: pow is the sound of an impact
entering means going in

explanation.surface: A flamboyant bird makes a splash on arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Powin is a Scots word for the peacock, the showiest of birds.

clue.text: The best of northern England, one of its rivers, if not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: the Swale is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Praise for the finest of the north and one of its rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wale is a northern English dialect word for the choicest, the pick.

clue.text: Heart in theatre grind or suffering bypass? (8, two words)

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked about, so the letters are rearranged
the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heart patient in the operating theatre, enduring a bypass operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' and 'bypass' paint surgery, but the bypass is a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road circles a town so traffic can avoid its centre, a bypass.

clue.text: Early dialect I don't understand, including odd elements of Gallic

indicators.note: including means holding inside

parts.note: anan is an old exclamation meaning 'what? I don't follow'

indicators.note: odd elements are the first, third and fifth letters

parts.note: letters one, three and five of Gallic

explanation.surface: Someone confused by an old dialect sprinkled with French.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglian was the Old English dialect of the Angles, spoken in the Midlands and north.

clue.text: High moorland was ruined by spades

parts.note: a city that fell was ruined
S is spades in card notation

explanation.surface: Upland moors spoilt by digging.
explanation.definitionFit: Fells are high open hills or moors in northern England.

clue.text: Plate by river showing those that may expect royalties?

parts.note: a paten is a plate for communion bread
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A silver plate found beside a river and handed over to the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Patentees hold patents and may earn royalties from those licensed to use the invention.
